title: Kingdom of Saxony
capsule: The Kingdom of Saxony was proclaimed on 20 December 1806 when Napoleon elevated Frederick Augustus III, the last Elector of Saxony, to King Frederick Augustus I as reward for Saxony's pivot to France following Prussian collapse at Jena-Auerstedt; Saxony joined the Confederation of the Rhine and became one of Napoleon's most loyal German client states. The Treaties of Tilsit in 1807 granted Frederick Augustus personal sovereignty over the newly created Duchy of Warsaw, making him a key pivot of Napoleon's eastern European order. Saxony fought alongside France at the Battle of Leipzig in October 1813 — nearly alone among German states — and the king was taken prisoner by the Prussians; the Congress of Vienna in 1815 punished this loyalty by transferring approximately 60 percent of Saxony's territory to Prussia.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The kingdom's territorial extent in 1806–1809 is well established from Napoleonic-era cartography and administrative records; the dataset window of 1806–1809 captures the earliest consolidation phase before the 1815 post-war truncation.
